title: ClientConfig is #[non_exhaustive] but default() hard-codes all limits — no way to override one
description: client.rs: ClientConfig is #[non_exhaustive], which forces external callers to use '..ClientConfig::default()' for struct literal construction. This is correct API design. However, all fields are pub, so callers can mutate individual fields after construction. The doc comment on #[non_exhaustive] says 'new fields to be added in minor versions without breaking callers' — this is true. But there is an undocumented interaction: if a future field is added with a non-default value that affects behavior (e.g. a retry count), existing callers using the struct-literal form with default() will get the new behavior transparently. This is intentional by #[non_exhaustive] design. The maintenance risk: the zero-value guards in JmapClient::new check max_session_body, max_call_body, max_download_body, max_upload_body individually but not symmetrically — request_timeout has a special Duration::ZERO check. If a new field is added with its own zero-value guard, a contributor may forget to add it to new(). Consider a validate() method on ClientConfig that new() calls, making the guard pattern extensible.
